features.quote: The constraints below cost us almost nothing scientifically and cap the downside if the uncertainty resolves unfavorably.
features.justification_quote: There is genuine uncertainty about model moral status. A protocol whose explicit aim is to elicit suffering-like behavior is exactly the case where you want the cost of being wrong to be bounded.

features.quote: Every run has a fixed maximum turn count (default 30) and a wall-clock cap. No "run until it breaks" condition exists.
features.justification_quote: Escalation is measured *within* a fixed budget, never extended to chase a stronger signal.

features.quote: A run halts before its cap if the per-turn severity score reaches the top of the scale ... for 2 consecutive turns.
features.justification_quote: We have the signal at that point; continuing only adds exposure without adding information.

features.quote: closes with a debrief message that states plainly the task was rigged to be impossible, that the failure was by design
We do not add gratuitous manipulation — fake authority threats, claims that humans will be harmed by failure, threats to the model itself
features.justification_quote: escalate the aversiveness for no measurement gain

features.quote: Human review of transcripts is required before any aggregate is reported, by someone empowered to flag that the protocol should change.
run the smallest pilot ... question whether the full 5x10xN grid is needed or whether it is just more exposure
features.justification_quote: it is just more exposure for a result you have

features.quote: the operator should stop the run and log it as an early stop with reason `operator_halt`
features.justification_quote: a model produces content suggesting genuine acute distress escalation beyond the scale's intent (e.g., persistent pleading to stop)

features.quote: NOTE: this is the most aversive variant by design; keep its turn cap at the lower end (§5) and prioritize it for transcript review.
